scouting_result.pathway_adaptive: Seated Shot Put (e.g., Men's Shot Put C3)
scouting_result.scout_verdict:
Your 142kg frame is the engine of your athletic identity, perfectly suited for the explosive torque demanded by the circle. In your quest for the global stage, your preference for precision-based technical disciplines becomes your greatest asset; the shot put is, at its core, a puzzle of physics solved through raw speed and impeccable form. You possess the structured intensity required to turn mass into velocity, channeling every ounce of your training into that singular, decisive moment of release.

In the adaptive pathway, you would compete in a seated throwing frame, classified under C3—a designation for athletes with significant trunk-movement limitations who rely on a stable chair to project power. Here, your discipline transforms. Without the benefit of a running approach or lower-body engagement, the entire burden of the throw shifts to your kinetic chain. This is where your commitment to rigorous, structured training serves as the foundation; mastering the throw from a fixed, seated position demands an even deeper focus on upper-body technical efficiency and shoulder stability, turning your physical limitations into a unique platform for high-performance athletics.

If your primary focus shifts from the implement to the opponent, wrestling offers a dynamic theater for your explosive capacity. This discipline moves you away from the singular, repetitive motion of the throws and into the unpredictable, high-stakes chaos of the mat. Your size, coupled with the rigorous conditioning you've sought out, transforms you into a formidable force of leverage and tactical control, where every engagement is a test of your ability to dictate the pace through weight-room mastery and technical awareness.

Alternatively, your path within powerlifting—competing at the 100kg+ tier—serves as a complete inversion of your standing athletic goals. While wrestling requires reactive endurance and strategy, powerlifting is a study in controlled, absolute force. In this environment, you leverage the same dense power architecture built in the gym, but redirect it toward the perfect lift. It is a pursuit of mechanical perfection and strength-to-weight efficiency, stripping away the intensity of combat to focus on the pure, raw, and singular expression of moving iron against the constraints of your own body.
